summary.text: Ali Rabe is a Democratic member of the Idaho Senate representing District 16, in the second term that the Idaho Legislature's membership page lists.
Rabe serves on the Local Government and Taxation and Transportation committees and is executive director of the Gem State Housing Alliance.

paragraphs.text: Rabe was born in Boise and raised in Middleton, and graduated from The College of Idaho with a B.A. in political economics, summa cum laude.
Rabe earned a J.D., cum laude, from William & Mary Law School and is a member of the Idaho State Bar.

Rabe's legislative biography lists Rabe as executive director of Gem State Housing Alliance, a statewide nonprofit dedicated to increasing housing supply, and a former executive director of Jesse Tree, a Treasure Valley nonprofit dedicated to preventing eviction and homelessness.

It also lists Rabe as a former staff attorney for communities addressing homelessness, a former asylum and refugee officer for the Department of Homeland Security, and a 2012 Boren Fellow, and as having worked for international nonprofits in Cambodia and Sierra Leone on protecting communities' agricultural land rights.
The biography also lists Rabe as a member of the board of trustees of The College of Idaho.
The biography says Rabe is married to Riley and has two sons.
